_readme: The capture harness's prompt corpus. One entry per scenario in the SHIM directive's coverage list. `prompt` is null exactly when the scenario has no prompt-only provocation; `manual` then states the operator step. See README.md.

_fields.name: Directory name under captures/. Stable: the mock's scenario registry keys off it.
_fields.covers: The coverage-list item this entry discharges.
_fields.prompt: The single user turn, or null for a manual scenario.
_fields.manual: The operator procedure, for a scenario a prompt cannot provoke (or cannot provoke alone).
_fields.manual_setup: An operator step needed BEFORE an otherwise prompt-driven turn.
_fields.cwd_setup: Files materialized in the scratch cwd before the turn: {path, content} or {path, dir: true}.
_fields.options: Extra SDK Options merged over the production options (maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, model, outputFormat, mcpServers). The token {{CAPTURE_DIR}} is replaced with scripts/capture/'s absolute path.
_fields.permission_script: {default, rules:[{tool, decision, message?, delay_ms?}]}; decision is allow_once | allow_standing | deny | park.
_fields.question_script: {answers:[{question, select:[label...], free_text?}]}; a question with no entry is left UNANSWERED.
_fields.controls: [{at: session_start|on_message|turn_end, after?: {type, subtype, contains}, do: <verb>, args}].
_fields.expect: What the capture must contain for the scenario to have discharged its coverage. Prose, read by a human at review time — not asserted by code.
_fields.expects_api_error: True only for a scenario whose GOLDEN is an API error. Every other scenario is quarantined if its result carries is_error / terminal_reason api_error / api_error_status, or if any message carries is_api_error_message.
_fields.expects_error_subtypes: Result subtypes this scenario's GOLDEN is allowed to end in with is_error true (e.g. ["error_max_turns"]). Never excuses an api_error terminal; use expects_api_error for that.
_fields.config_root: "shared-world:<name>": scenarios naming the same world share ONE cwd and account root and run in corpus order, so a later scenario sees what the earlier ones did. Absent = an isolated world of its own.
_fields.prompts: An ordered array of turns, instead of `prompt`. Each entry is a string, or { text, resume: true } to close the query and reopen it resuming the same vendor session id.
_fields.cwd_init: A shell command run in the scratch cwd BEFORE the query (e.g. `git init`). A non-zero exit fails the scenario.
_fields.resume_capture: The directory name of a capture ALREADY IN testdata/captures/ whose vendor session this scenario resumes. That session is as cold as its commit date, so resuming it is a genuinely LAPSED prompt cache — the one thing a same-process `resume: true` turn cannot be. The capture's own cwd is read from its transcript (which records it verbatim) and recreated, and its transcript is seeded into the run's THROWAWAY account root, so this requires --seed-credentials.

scenarios.name: api-error-classes
scenarios.covers: the API error classes (ApiRequestFailed's taxonomy), including a 429
scenarios.manual: No prompt provokes these. Capture each by driving the SDK against a deliberately broken API path: (a) 429 — run a burst of concurrent sessions on a rate-limited account, or capture the `rate_limit_event` message and `system:api_error` line the vendor emits when the account's window is exhausted; (b) 401/403 — run once with an invalid credential in the scratch CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; (c) 500/overloaded — capture opportunistically, or point the SDK at a proxy that returns 529; (d) connection failure — run with the network down. Each run's `system:api_error` line and `api_retry` message is the golden.

scenarios.manual: Auto-compaction fires on WINDOW OCCUPANCY, not on a prompt, and the 2026-09-03 attempts showed a tiny `autoCompactWindow` alone does not provoke it (occupancy never left ~45k). This entry instead PACES real occupancy upward: sixteen turns, each reading one 40000-byte file (~10k tokens) in full, so the transcript climbs ~10k per turn toward the 200k window and crosses the auto-compact threshold between turns rather than blowing past the window inside one turn (which is what an 80000-byte-per-file corpus read in one turn does: it 400s with `terminal_reason: prompt_too_long`). The two goldens are the `system:status` message whose status is `compacting` (START) and the `system:compact_boundary` line (END).
